study: Portes et al. 2018 (Instructional Conversation / IC efficacy RCT; AERJ 55(3); IES R305A100670)
eval_evidence: Authored/conducted by the IC research team (Portes et al., Univ. of Georgia) under their own IES grant; developer-run efficacy trial and analyses, no independent evaluator (the paper's PD-comparison table notes prior IC studies' experimental teachers were 'part of research team').
developer_evidence: The research team provided the intensive 100-hour assisted-teaching PD; 'Trained coaches provided additional support and feedback' (p.~12) -- the team's own trained coaches delivered the program.
cascade_evidence: The research team and its own trained coaches delivered the 100h assisted-teaching PD directly to treatment teachers; no separate intermediary organization between developer and teachers -> developer_direct.
counterfactual_evidence: p.~12: 'Control teachers (N=34) were also provided incentives to conduct business-as-usual teaching'; BAU control monitored via logs/videos.
coaching_evidence: Intensive 100-hour program of ASSISTED TEACHING in the teachers' own classrooms during the practice year, with trained coaches providing ongoing support/feedback and collecting monthly implementation evaluations -> recurring in-class coaching cycles (frequent_inclass).
student_dose_evidence: IC reorganizes the TEACHER'S OWN instruction into small-group dialogic lessons (1-2x/week, ~30 min, taught by the regular teacher); it is a pedagogical change in the teacher's regular instruction, not an added third-party tutoring/pull-out dose -> none.
maturity_evidence: Treatment teachers completed a full PD 'practice year' implementing IC BEFORE the efficacy year; student outcomes were collected in the second ('efficacy') year, so teachers had >=1 prior implementation year -> mature.
